core_obligations: Reduce to bounded complexes (proof lines 14365-14368): the cohomology H^i(K tensor^L L) only depends on the truncations tau_{>= i-1}K and tau_{>= i-1}L, so it suffices to treat the case where K and L are bounded.

Replace by complexes of locally constant sheaves (proof lines 14369-14372): by the cited representation lemma, for bounded K and L one may assume they are represented by complexes of locally constant sheaves of Lambda-modules of finite type.

Replace by finite free modules and conclude (proof lines 14372-14374): over a site the locally constant sheaves of finite type in question can be replaced by bounded above complexes of finite free Lambda-modules, and for those the tensor product visibly has locally constant finite type cohomology, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Use truncations to reduce to bounded complexes.
Use the representation lemma to reduce to complexes of locally constant finite type sheaves.
Replace those by complexes of finite free modules, where the statement is immediate.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that over a site with a Noetherian ring Lambda, if K and L are bounded above complexes of Lambda-modules whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant of finite type, then the cohomology sheaves of the derived tensor product K tensor^L L are again locally constant of finite type (statement lines 14355-14363). The proof (proof lines 14365-14376) makes three reductions: to bounded complexes by truncation, to complexes of locally constant finite type sheaves by the representation lemma, and to complexes of finite free modules where the claim is immediate. H2: a three-step reduction with two inputs, written out in full.
